Hi Samantha — answering the bullets with concrete notes; copied the small JSON/webhook snippet inline and attached the full json-contract-horizon-v1.json.

1) KV cache: by default the runtime keeps in-memory KV for active sessions; durable caching is optional and configurable per deployment. We can set "kv_persistence": false for the Horizon staging project so no cache touches disk. Runbook includes commands to toggle this. (See runbook-kvcache.md attachment.)

2) Function-call validation: you can enable HMAC signing on the function-call payloads. We support an HMAC header (X-Redwood-Sig) and public key rotation. Example (signed response header):

    X-Redwood-Sig: sha256=4f7af2...

We also support mutual TLS for server-to-server webhook calls if you're using our private deployment.

3) Webhook example (minimal):

POST /horizon-ingest HTTP/1.1
Host: ingest.horizonhealth.com
Authorization: Bearer <token>
Content-Type: application/json
X-Redwood-Sig: sha256=<signature>

Body: {
  "request_id": "req_12345",
  "payload": {
    "patient_id": "string",
    "action": "summary",
    "structured_output": {
      "diagnosis_codes": ["I10"],
      "confidence": 0.92
    }
  }
}

Max recommended payload: 256 KB for webhook POST; for larger outputs we recommend chunked streaming to a pre-signed URL.

I can also prepare a short canary scripts repo and a small automated test that validates signature + schema.
